newsitem.title: USA: Florida researchers say mower will cut grass smartly.
newsitem.headline: Florida researchers say mower will cut grass smartly.

text.p: It may be the ultimate suburbanite dream -- stretching out in a hammock with a cool drink while a robot cuts the grass.
A robot lawn mower called the LawnNibbler will do the work and avoid obstacles like dogs, kids, trees and other lawn clutter, University of Florida researchers said Wednesday.
The machine, operated by computers and powered by a rechargeable battery, uses a nylon cutting cord similar to those in lawn trimmers now on the market.
A radio wire buried at the perimeter of the yard and a navigational beacon system using sonar and infrared emitters and detectors will keep it on track, researchers said.

"Previous attempts at robot lawnmowers were limited because of the absence of a navigation system," Kevin Hakala, a graduate student who developed the machine at UF's Machine Intelligence Lab, said in a statement.
"Because of the beacon navigation system, LawnNibbler knows where it is," he said.
The machine's sonar and infrared system will allow it to avoid obstacles and know where it has already cut, researchers said.
In mass production, the robot lawnmower could sell for $600-$1,000, lab director Keith Doty said. The university is searching for venture capital.
There are still bugs to be worked out and social issues to consider, Doty said. "For example, what if it gets out of control and goes on your neighbour's lawn or flowers?"
UF researchers also are working on a vacuum cleaner using the same technology.
